newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. treasuries.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in quiet trade on Wednesday, taking much of their direction from U.S. treasuries, with the lingering weight of recent new issues also hurting prices, analysts said.

"We opened up unchanged then weakened off with the U.S. market. It definitely felt like there was fairly heavy selling pressure in Canada, even though volumes have been pretty light," said one bond trader with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$115.84 to yield 6.759 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.73 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to three basis points from two basis points at Tuesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. bond markets opened weaker this morning with consolidation and some profit taking happening in both markets. Traders in both markets are also looking ahead to the release later this afternoon of the Fed Beige Book.
In Canada, analysts said recent new issues which have not been fully distributed also continued to weigh on prices. Both Ontario and Quebec recently tapped the domestic market for new borrowing.
"It may take a few more days to get all this product distributed because volumes have not really been all that high," the trader said.
Canadian manufacturing and wholesale trade data for April released this morning had little impact on prices, dealers said.

Analysts said Canadian fixed-income markets are now looking ahead to a speech and news press conference by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen in Quebec City. Thiessen begins speaking at 1215 EDT/1615 GMT and is expected to hold his press conference at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.10 to C$107.82 to yield 6.184 percent while the U.S. 10-year traded unchanged to yield 6.43 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 26 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.83 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.06 percent.
